title: Does an extremal surface always exist for a chain in a closed surface group?
body:
## The question

Let S be a closed hyperbolic surface and C a chain in pi_1(S). An admissible surface for
C of degree n is extremal if it realises scl(C), that is, if -chi^-(S')/(2n) = scl(C).

Does an extremal surface always exist?

One case is settled, and positively. If C is disjoint from some simple essential curve on
S, then cutting along that curve reduces the problem to a graph of free groups amalgamated
over cyclic subgroups, and the relevant theorem produces not only rationality but an
extremal surface. So any counterexample must involve a chain that cannot be pushed off
every simple essential curve.

This is a question and not a conjecture, and the two should not be confused. Rationality
of scl for chains in closed hyperbolic surface groups is definitely conjectured to hold.
The existence of extremal surfaces is not: it could easily be false in general, and a
counterexample would not bear against rationality.
